qs: What is the “Babylonian system”? How can I tell whether I’m living inside it?
Does “come out of Babylon” mean I should quit my job, move house or delete my social media accounts?
Daniel was in Babylon but not of Babylon. How can I learn from him at work?
The blood of the Lamb, the word of our testimony, not loving our lives — which of these three keys am I most lacking?
How can I practise the Three Foundations — Jesus is my role model, the Bible is my standard, the Holy Spirit is my guide — every day?
What does it really mean to take Jesus as my role model? Is it copying his actions, or something more?
The Bible is my standard — but how do I decide about things the Bible doesn’t directly address?
How do I know whether it’s the Holy Spirit guiding me or just my own thoughts?
What does “let Jesus be King” actually look like in a marriage?
In my ministry, how can I tell whether I’m letting Jesus receive the glory or just wanting to be seen myself?
How is “establish God’s system” different from planting a church?
Can my home become God’s system? Where do I start?
What does the end time revival have to do with an ordinary believer like me?
Is revival something we wait for, or something we walk out?
Of the three tiers of revival — personal, church and kingdom — where am I stuck right now?
How can I apply the fivefold change — mindset, life, daily living, relationships and ministry — to myself?
I’m often moved by a sermon but can’t live it out. Where is the problem?
Why do we say “change begins with me”? What can I change first?
Why fast and pray every week? My health isn’t good — what can I do?
Please help me remember the heart of this unit in one sentence.

qs: What does “see no one but Jesus” mean? How do I live that out at church?
I deeply respect my pastor. Is that “lifting up a person”? Where is the line?
I tend to rely on a spiritual elder to make my decisions. How do I turn to relying on Jesus instead?
“Seeing self brings the fall” — but aren’t we also meant to know ourselves?
I’m often afraid of what others think of me. What does that have to do with “seeing self”?
Why does comparison bring separation? I only want to improve.
There’s a wall of suspicion in my heart towards a co-worker in ministry. How can I tear it down?
I know I should forgive, but I can’t get past the feelings. What do I do?
Can I even see the wall of self-centredness in myself?
How is “lay down self, no more separation” different from being a people-pleaser with no boundaries?
What is the “Whose Is It?” lesson asking? Whose are my time, my money and my children?
“By whom? For whom?” — how do I check my motives for serving?
The focus is on Jesus, not on myself, others or circumstances — even when circumstances are truly awful?
When Jesus is lifted up, people are hidden — so should I still use my gifts?
How can I help a brother who keeps putting a particular speaker on a pedestal, without hurting him?
What would “seeing only Jesus” change in my family?
Someone in my small group keeps comparing who’s more spiritual. How can I respond?
How do I tell the difference between unity and compromise?
Once the walls of separation come down, how do we rebuild the relationship?
Please help me remember the heart of this unit in one sentence.

qs: “Out of it is the wellspring of life” — how are the heart and the brain different?
Won’t “let the heart govern the brain” turn into acting on feelings?
If God looks at the heart, does outward behaviour not matter?
What is a simple heart? Am I not simple-hearted if I overthink things?
How do I keep a clear conscience? I’m always blaming myself.
What’s the difference between a sincere faith and forcing myself to believe?
What difference in outcome is there between relying on the heart and the effort of relying on the brain?
Fix my eyes on Jesus — what exactly am I to look at in him?
“Winning the heart matters more than the task” — but somebody still has to get the job done, right?
If the church is a family, not a company, does it need structures and efficiency at all?
When a crisis comes, how can I turn it into a chance to win hearts?
How is winning hearts to make whole different from pleasing people?
When I lead my small group I always rush to get through the programme and overlook the people. How do I adjust?
How can I tell whether my heart has drifted away from God?
Rely on the heart and the Holy Spirit, not on the brain and ourselves — my job demands a lot of thinking, so how do I keep the balance?
What does “rely on the heart and you’re glad; rely on the brain and you worry” mean?
How do I “rely on the heart” with my family?
How should I pray for someone whose heart is wounded?
How can I walk alongside a brother or sister whose heart has grown cold?
Please help me remember the heart of this unit in one sentence.

qs: Why is a change of mindset necessary? I’ve been a believer for years — does my mindset still need to change?
What are the eight stages of changing our mindset? Which stage am I at right now?
What’s the difference between “Information” and “Revelation”?
I often get stuck at the “Conviction” stage. How do I break through?
I put things into practice for a few days and then give up. How do I walk the “Repetition” stage?
What’s the difference between evaluation and self-blame?
What does “Multiplication” mean? What can I multiply?
“A renewed mindset holds new wine” — how do I know whether my wineskin is old?
Can you give an everyday example of changing from a human point of view to God’s point of view?
How does changing from a temporary perspective to an eternal one affect the decisions I make today?
How is the concept of humility different from low self-esteem?
Suffering is a blessing in disguise — I’m suffering right now, so how can I see the blessing?
God dares to use people who fall — so can I still be used after I’ve fallen?
“God uses those who know they can’t” — but what if I’m very capable?
I’m willing to be used by God, but the opportunity never comes. Is the problem me?
What’s the difference between Satan’s concept of marriage and God’s concept of marriage?
Does “the two become one flesh” still hold when we’re arguing?
My spouse isn’t a believer. How can we “make each other whole”?
“Change begins with action” — what is one action I can take today?
Please help me remember the heart of this unit in one sentence.

qs: What is “the self-centred life”? What is “selflessness”?
Doesn’t selflessness mean having no self? Then what about my personality and my gifts?
“‘Self’ is the root of our fall” — can you explain that from the Bible?
What does “let go of sovereignty, let Jesus reign” look like at work?
Let Jesus build his church — then what are we co-workers supposed to do?
I deny myself today and grab it all back tomorrow. How do I “hold to denying of self”?
What’s the difference between denying myself and just putting up with being wronged?
“For Jesus, for others, not for self” — won’t that mean I stop looking after myself?
How can selflessness lead into fullness? It sounds like a loss.
How does selflessness bring victory? Victory over what?
Is “‘I’ no longer live, but Christ lives in me” a feeling or a choice?
How can I tell whether today’s decision is self-centred or selfless?
Only selflessness can bring unity — how do I apply that when my small group disagrees?
Can you explain the saying “selflessness overcomes Satan”?
Practising selflessness at home — what small thing should I start with?
I’m worn out by ministry. Is that because I’m living the self-centred life?
Won’t selfless people get taken advantage of?
How are selflessness and humility related?
How can I walk alongside a brother with a strong “self” rather than fighting him?
Please help me remember the heart of this unit in one sentence.

qs: Why do we say that sin is the fruit of pride?
Where does pride come from? I can’t see pride in myself.
What does “I have, and I don’t want” mean?
Where do sinful desires come from? How do I close the door to sin and open the door to God?
Humility is the antidote to pride — how do I “take” this medicine?
How can humility be a strategy for victory? Isn’t it just backing down?
“Turn the other cheek, go the extra mile” — even when I’m being bullied at work?
“Lay down our rights, return to our originally intended position” — what is my originally intended position?
What does laying down the right to be God mean? I’ve never wanted to be God.
If I lay down the right to glory, how should I respond when people affirm me?
How do I let Jesus be seen instead of me?
What are the three movements of hiddenness?
Laying down the right over life and death — what does that have to do with my life today?
Laying down the right to be respected — but being humiliated really hurts.
Won’t unconditional acceptance just let the other person off the hook?
From human rule back to God’s rule — does that conflict with what people mean by human rights today?
“Let man be man and let God be God” — I often overstep without realising it. What should I do?
Which is easier — humility or pride?
What are the three sayings for practising humility daily? How can I use them?
Please help me remember the heart of this unit in one sentence.

qs: What does “from ‘I can’ to ‘I already am’” mean?
How do I live out “no longer I” every morning?
How does a change of choices establish God’s system?
Two trees, two systems — how can I tell which tree I’m eating from?
What is the first step back to God’s system?
Choose humility — even when the other person is clearly in the wrong?
Choosing to rely on the Holy Spirit versus choosing to rely on my own effort — how do they feel different?
Choose faith, choose love — how do I choose when I’m afraid?
Why do we say “every choice matters”? Do small things count too?
Selflessness is not hard — so why does it feel so hard to me?
“Not combating, but cultivating” — so I don’t need to deal with my bad habits?
Denying of self has to be daily — how do I keep it from going numb and becoming a ritual?
From what age can my children start learning to deny themselves?
Does denying of self conflict with a healthy sense of self-worth?
Will I still have dreams once I deny myself?
What does denying of self look like in church decision-making?
How can I walk alongside a companion who is learning to deny himself but keeps failing?
Denying of self or letting Jesus be King — which comes first?
How can I use the eight stages to take denying of self deeper?
Please help me remember the heart of this unit in one sentence.

qs: What is revival? Does it have to do with bigger attendance?
What is “living out the life of Jesus”? Could you be more concrete?
Which is the main thing — nurturing life or dealing with sin?
Why do seeing, listening, thinking, speaking and doing matter? Does their order mean anything?
What does “seeing rightly” mean we should look at?
How do I let God open my eyes?
Is “what we see, we receive” just prosperity theology?
How do I listen only to God’s voice? There are so many voices in my head.
Listen rightly and life changes — how do I know I’ve heard rightly?
Hear clearly, discern truly, walk surely — how do I practise these three steps?
How do I become good soil?
“Thinking rightly” — I often think negatively. How do I change?
“Thinking is a process of conceiving” — so what am I conceiving?
What does “conceive only Christ” mean?
How do I tell right speaking from wrong speaking?
Truth on the lips, love in the heart — won’t telling the truth hurt people?
What’s missing between knowing and doing?
“Do it, then understand” — but I’d rather understand first and then act.
Do it from the heart and in love it’s not hard — is it really not hard in love?
How do I form habits and live as a new creation?

qs: Why do we say the centre of God’s will is building relationships?
How is building relationships in love different from pleasing people?
What is the priority of relationships? Why God first, then ourselves, then others?
What does “our relationship with ourselves” mean? Do I need to love myself?
How can I let God’s love flow to people I don’t like?
“Get people right and things come right” — but doing things badly isn’t acceptable either, is it?
Rectify the priority: my priorities are a mess. Where do I start sorting them out?
“Get relationships right and everything comes right” — could you give an example?
Discipline is for restoration — how should I discipline my children or my team members?
What does “throw a rope, not a stone” mean?
People matter more than tasks — but my job demands efficiency.
Relationships matter more than things — how do I apply that when we argue about money as a couple?
How can I mend a broken relationship when the other person won’t speak to me?
What is the 920 practice? How can I begin?
Who is my “2”? Is everyone one?
What is 235? How do I find a spiritual companion?
How are relationships between spiritual parents and spiritual children built?
How do we build real relationships in a small group, not just hold meetings?
I’m an introvert and building relationships is hard for me. What should I do?
Please help me remember the heart of this unit in one sentence.

qs: What is service? Does it only count if I hold a position in the church?
Whose need is service? Isn’t it others who need me?
Why do we say “service is my own need”?
Who can serve? I don’t feel qualified.
What do the stages of the Path of Serving — Spirit, Understanding, Life, Service, God — mean?
Why does serving begin with the Holy Spirit rather than with the need?
How do I mind the Holy Spirit? Can the Holy Spirit be grieved?
From the letter into revelation — when I read the Bible I often just skim past the words.
From knowing into living it out — how is this unit different from what came before?
What does denying of self without holding back look like in ministry?
What’s the difference between service that lets Jesus be King and service that makes myself king?
Passing on life and multiplying disciples — how can I begin discipling one person?
Let Jesus receive all the glory — how should I respond when I’m praised for my service?
How do I put “see no one but Jesus” into practice in ministry?
What is a fivefold-ministry team? Which role suits me?
What should I do when serving is exhausting and I want to give up?
How do I tell God’s calling apart from my own zeal?
How can I walk alongside a young person who has just started serving?
When ministry and family clash, how do I choose?
Please help me remember the heart of the whole Living Out 321 series in one sentence.
